chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi narrated to us, saying: Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Ghalib narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Rabah narrated to us, from Saif ibn Umairah, who said: Muhammad ibn Marwan narrated to us, who said: Abdullah ibn Abi Ya'foor narrated to us, from Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon them both, who said:

Three persons' prayers are not accepted by Allah: a slave who has run away from his masters until he returns to them and places his hand in their hands; a man who leads a people in prayer while they despise him; and a woman who passes the night while her husband is displeased with her.

key_terms.آبِق: A runaway slave (abiq) — one who has fled from their master without permission
key_terms.أَمَّ قَوْمًا: Led a people (in prayer) — acted as imam for a congregation
key_terms.سَاخِط: Displeased/angry (sakhit) — in a state of displeasure or wrath
key_terms.مَوَالِيهِ: His masters/patrons (mawali) — those who have authority or guardianship over someone

ai.seo_question: According to Imam al-Sadiq, whose prayers does Allah not accept?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (as) identifies three categories of people whose prayers are not accepted by Allah: a runaway slave, an imam leading unwilling congregants, and a wife who sleeps while her husband is angry with her. This ruling emphasizes the Islamic principle that valid worship requires fulfilling one's social and contractual obligations. In its original context, this teaching addressed a society where communal prayer and household relationships carried legal and spiritual weight, and the three examples illustrate how neglecting duties to others undermines the sincerity and acceptance of one's worship.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 2. He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji’abi reported to me from Abul Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who reported from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Ghalib, who reported from al-Husayn ibn ‘Ali ibn Rabah, from Saif ibn Umairah, who reported from Muhammad ibn Marwan, who reported from Abdullah ibn Abi Ya’foor that: Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad, peace be upon him, said: "

Allah does not bless the prayers with acceptance from three persons: From a slave who has escaped from his masters, till he returns and places his hand in their hands; from an Imam who leads people (in prayers) while they hate him; from a wife who passes a night while her husband is displeased with her."
